chooseChecklist.title: Regulation first
chooseChecklist.text: Check which regulator supervises the entity you are actually onboarding with. The licence on the homepage is not always the licence on the account you open.

chooseChecklist.title: Demo before live
chooseChecklist.text: Run the system on a demo account at that broker first. Spread, swap and execution differ enough between brokers to change how a scalping strategy behaves.

chooseChecklist.title: Spread and execution cost
chooseChecklist.text: Automated scalping lives or dies on execution cost. A raw-spread account with a commission is often cheaper than a marked-up spread account.

chooseChecklist.title: Minimum deposit vs account size
chooseChecklist.text: A low minimum deposit is not a recommended account size. Check the system's own minimum equity before choosing a broker around a $10 deposit.

chooseChecklist.title: MT4 or MT5 support
chooseChecklist.text: Confirm the platform your licence runs on is available at that broker, and that expert advisors are permitted on the account type you pick.

faqs.question: How did you choose these brokers?
faqs.answer: They are the platforms we test our own expert advisors on. The comparison lists regulation, minimum deposit, platforms and account types so you can match a broker to the system you intend to run, rather than ranking them on a single score.

faqs.question: Do you earn from these links?
faqs.answer: Yes. Some links on this page are affiliate links, and we may earn a commission if you open an account through one, at no extra cost to you. It does not change what is listed here or which systems we publish.

faqs.question: Is a lower minimum deposit better?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. The minimum deposit is the smallest amount the broker will open an account with, not a recommended trading balance. Our systems publish their own recommended minimum equity, and several need $1,000 or more to size positions properly.

faqs.question: What do the deposit bonuses mean?
faqs.answer: A deposit bonus is the broker's own promotion and comes with its own terms, turnover requirements and withdrawal conditions. Read those terms at the broker. A bonus is not profit and does not reduce the risk of trading.

faqs.question: Which broker should I run an expert advisor on?
faqs.answer: One with a regulation you are comfortable with, tight spreads on the instrument the system trades, and reliable execution. If you are unsure, start on a demo account at two brokers and compare the fills on the same strategy before committing capital.

faqs.question: Can I use a broker that is not on this list?
faqs.answer: Yes. Our systems run on any MetaTrader 4 or MetaTrader 5 broker. The list here is what we test on, not a restriction — though a low-spread ECN account will usually suit these strategies better than a high-spread one.

faqs.question: How much money do I need to start trading forex?
faqs.answer: Many brokers accept $1 to $10, but the useful question is how much lets you risk 1 to 2% per trade at a workable lot size. Practise on a demo account first, then fund only money you can afford to lose.

faqs.question: How do I check that a forex broker is regulated?
faqs.answer: Find the licence number on the broker's website, then search for it on the regulator's own public register and match the company name. Confirm the licence covers your country, and check the regulator's warning list.

faqs.question: Are high-leverage brokers better?
faqs.answer: No. Leverage magnifies losses as well as gains, so a higher limit is not a quality signal. Judge a broker on regulation, total cost and execution first, and size positions to your own risk.
